findings.where: First screen, the hero band's ground (desktop and phone), set against the palette tile and the texture tile below
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pale blue-to-lilac-to-pink gradient. That brings in a violet/pink hue found nowhere in the house colours, although the page's own palette tile says 'three colours, no accent' and its texture tile says 'the paper is a flat warm tone'. The gradient band also leaves a visible seam with the warm paper of the header above it and the specimen below it, so the first screen and the rest of the page read as two different sites.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for a look built in or around #0070C0 and #404040, with one soft ground and the house colours as the only ink. A development-bank visitor would also object: a pastel tech gradient reads as a SaaS landing page, slick rather than legal, which is what the brief rules out as 'in-your-face techy' and 'slick'.

findings.where: Margin notes beside the hero (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024) and the specimen section labels (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The house blue does two jobs. It marks every link and action, and it also colours static margin notes and labels that do nothing when clicked (the parts map lists all of these as static). Talk titles in link blue, sitting next to the 'Articles and Presentations' nav, look like links to those talks.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks 'Best Practices in PPP Legislation…' expecting the talk and nothing happens. They are left unsure which blue text is actionable, including the real links.

findings.where: Actions and links across the page: the hero 'Write to me' / 'Book a consultation' buttons, the article's 'Download' button, the hero address and the footer address
findings.fault: Like controls are styled unlike each other. The hero buttons are square-cornered blue fills, but the article's Download is a pill with a blue outline. The email address is ink with a grey underline in the hero but blue with a blue underline in the footer. There is no single treatment for 'this is an action' or 'this is a link'.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who needs one button style and one link style to reuse when she publishes. A visitor also has to learn three looks for the same kind of thing, which weakens the 'one action' read.

findings.where: The exhibit photograph in the hero and in the motion sketch, compared with the article's radio-interview photograph
findings.fault: The hero portrait has a wide soft drop shadow, but the article photograph is set flat on the paper. A static photo is given elevation in one place and not the other, so the page has no consistent rule for how a framed artefact sits.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding images to articles: she cannot tell which treatment a photograph should get. A careful reader may also read the shadowed portrait as a card that can be clicked.
